label: Ask Brandt what the parts are for
text: Brandt doesn't look up from the clipboard. "Precision fittings. Don't concern yourself."
note: Brandt won't say what the parts are for. Nobody here likes questions.

label: Look at the crate stencil
text: Fresh stencil on every lid: HWA, and a plain eagle beneath it. Heereswaffenamt. The Army Ordnance Office.
note: The crates are stencilled HWA: the Army Ordnance Office.

label: Read the newspaper
text: Front page: a long column of field guns on a muddy road, moving east. The headline promises the war will be over by Christmas.
note: The paper is full of field guns going east.

label: Talk to Emil at the break
text: Emil wipes his hands and keeps his voice low. "Ask yourself who pays for steel this year."
note: Emil: ask yourself who pays for steel this year.

label: Ask Emil about the drawing in his locker
text: Emil unfolds a creased drawing. A fitting is circled in pencil, seated inside a breech block. "Ours. Recognise it?"
note: The part is a breech-block fitting. For guns.

label: Look at the rail car
text: A goods wagon at the loading door, our crates going in. Chalked on the side: SMOLENSK.
note: The crates go by rail to Smolensk.

label: Read the circular on Brandt's desk
text: From the Ministry: thanks to Werk 7 for its part in supplying the guns of the Eastern campaign. Targets for the coming quarter will rise.
note: The Ministry thanks Werk 7 for the guns in the East. Quotas will rise.

label: Look at the new barracks
text: Behind the yard, a new barracks with a wire fence and a guard at the gate. The men going in wear a "P" patch on their jackets.
note: New barracks behind the yard. Wire, a guard, a "P" on every jacket.

label: Talk to Jakub
text: Jakub's German is careful. He kept the books for a sawmill near Kielce. In the spring the police closed the square and took every man of working age onto a train. He tells it plainly, then turns back to his press.
note: Jakub was taken from his town square onto a train. He did not choose to come here.

label: Ask Emil about bench 9
text: "Two men worked bench 9 before me. They complained about the hours, then about the contract. One Monday they weren't there. Nobody asked where."
note: Two men from bench 9 complained. Then they were gone.

label: Read the statement
text: Typed, single-spaced: Emil Krause, bench 9, has made remarks undermining production and spoken against the war effort. Greta has left a space for the witness's signature. Men named in statements like this one do not come back to the floor.
note: Greta's statement would take Emil off the floor for good.

label: Ask Brandt who the parts are really for
text: Brandt shuts the office door before he answers. "You know who we work for. Everyone knows."
note: Brandt: everyone knows who we work for.

label: Ask Emil what he does at the gauge
text: Emil taps the gauge, just past the edge of the green. "Here. It passes at the bench. It doesn't pass under load." He goes back to his press without another word.
note: Emil: a part pressed just outside the green passes at the bench and fails under load.
